depiction.primary_object: diagonal cross or X mark inside a circle
depiction.composition: centered X inside a circular outline

ambiguity: As a pure UI action glyph, it looks like a button to delete or cancel the to-do item itself rather than representing the topic of the task; also visually close to a rotated plus-in-circle.

modifier_semantics.meaning: status badge or action button boundary

task_intents: revoke access permissions for former user

Terminate the lawn care service contract before the spring auto-renewal

Stop the recurring monthly transfer to the old savings account

Withdraw application for the senior product role at Acme
Discontinue the legacy v1 API endpoints after the client migration
Call the gym on 5th Street to cancel membership before the annual fee hits on Friday
Send formal notice to terminate the coworking desk lease at the end of next month

near_misses.better: plus in circle or user plus

reasoning: A circled X is universal UI chrome for 'close', 'delete', or 'clear'. Next to a task in a to-do list it looks like a button to delete or cancel the task itself rather than representing the task's subject, and even for cancellation tasks the specific object being cancelled (flight, card, gym, app) is almost always a better cue.
